key_provisions.before: Adopted the Large Load Customer Regulation Act and changed cryptocurrency mining and data center provisions. Requires large-load interconnection standards, study fees, cost allocation to large-load customers, curtailment procedures, annual data center reports on electricity demand, water use, incentives, energy measures, renewable commitments, and service life, plus decommissioning-cost responsibility and community benefit agreements for data centers.
key_provisions.after: Adopted the Large Load Customer Regulation Act for new or expanded retail-load interconnections exceeding 20 MW at one site, with interconnection standards, study fees, cost/risk allocation and curtailment procedures. A separate data-center definition in section 70-1506 uses peak demand of at least 10 MW. That section provides utility cost/load-study powers and requires annual owner/operator reports by September 30 to the Department of Water, Energy, and Environment and Natural Resources Committee, full decommissioning-cost responsibility and community benefit agreements with affected communities. The retained compiled statute identifies July 18, 2026 as section 70-1506’s effective date; that date is not generalized to every provision, and act-wide present force remains unverified.

key_provisions.before: Proposed annual data center load reporting to the Nebraska Power Review Board, public power service terms for large data centers, cost-shift protections, decommissioning resources, and community benefit agreements. PRB minutes state committee amendments removed the annual PRB data center report from the LB1010 package.
key_provisions.after: Introduced proposal: annual statewide data-center load reporting by the representative organization to the Power Review Board; service-cost/risk, decommissioning and community-benefit terms for a separately defined large data center (peak demand of at least 20 MW); and supplier-website disclosures. Direct comparison with enacted LB1010 shows a different data-center class starting at 10 MW, annual operator reports to the Department of Water, Energy, and Environment and Natural Resources Committee, and revised cost/decommissioning terms. The proposed section 70-1025 PRB-report amendment is absent from retained LB1010. AM2422 (dated March 3, filed March 6 and adopted March 12, 2026) contains the 10 MW definition and annual owner/operator reporting requirement on printed pages 17–18. The PRB March 20 minutes explicitly confirm committee removal of the proposed annual report to the PRB, but do not establish the reason for that removal. AM2422 is an intermediary amendment, not the final enacted text.

key_provisions.before: Revenue measure changing disclosure of tax information to municipalities, including disclosure requirements applicable to certain large data-center incentive agreements. The act also reproduces tier 2 large data-center provisions concerning local sales/use tax refunds and exemptions; whether the changed language imposes an additional data-center incentive condition remains unresolved.
key_provisions.after: Municipal tax-information disclosure measure. Section 1 changes municipal access to tax records and permits defined limited sharing. Section 2 adds a municipal request for lists of incentive applicants and reorganizes the existing annual incentive-disclosure provisions. Section 3 carries forward the tier-2 large-data-center investment/employment, exemption and refund terms while changing section 77-5725(3)(a)’s disclosure cross-reference from section 77-27,144(6) to (7). Visual review of the marked section identifies no added data-center investment or hiring threshold. These are enacted-version text observations; provision-specific effectiveness and later force remain unverified.

key_provisions.before: Would have prohibited any person, business, or entity from beginning construction of a new data center in New Hampshire from the effective date through 1 year after enactment. It also would have created a study committee on environmental impacts.
key_provisions.after: Introduced HB1265 would prohibit beginning construction of a new data center from the act’s effective date through one year following, and create a study committee on environmental impacts. The introduced act proposes effectiveness 60 days after passage; the one-year construction interval is anchored to that effective date, not enactment. No operative moratorium or actual effective/end date is asserted for this failed proposal.

key_provisions.before: Would create RSA chapter 374-I for large-energy-use retail electricity facilities. Covered facilities include 20 MW or more peak demand and NAICS 518210 uses, including computer processing, data processing centers, and web hosting. The PUC would create a separate tariff class and cost-shifting protections.
key_provisions.after: Introduced HB1722 would create RSA chapter 374-I for facilities that both can use at least 20 MW at peak demand and are primarily engaged in NAICS 518210 services, including computer processing, data processing centers and web hosting. It proposes a separate PUC retail-service class and tariff, cost-allocation/ratepayer protections, minimum 10-year service contracts with billing and termination protections, and an initial tariff docket by January 1, 2028. These are proposed obligations, not operative tariffs.

key_provisions.before: Would create RSA chapter 162-V to attract large-scale data-center campuses through municipal property-tax stabilization or PILOT authority, transferable business tax credits capped at 20 percent of construction costs, grid modernization agreements, cost-sharing, non-gas generation procurement, fast-track industrial and brownfield siting, host-community agreements, noise limits, setbacks, resident bill credits, and workforce provisions.
key_provisions.after: Introduced HB1739 would create RSA chapter 162-V for large-scale data-center campuses, with municipal property-tax stabilization or PILOT agreements, transferable business-tax credits, grid modernization agreements and cost-sharing/non-gas generation procurement, fast-track industrial/brownfield siting, host-community agreements, noise/setbacks, resident bill credits and workforce provisions. The credit text states a percentage of construction costs subject to a statewide cap of 20 percent of total construction costs. The appended fiscal note flags ambiguity in the credit/cap, tax interactions and administration; a fixed 20 percent per-project entitlement is not established. No proposed incentive or obligation is asserted as enacted.

key_provisions.before: As introduced, would add RSA 674:81-83, define data centers, and authorize municipalities to permit data centers in commercial or industrial zones with utility capacity confirmation, noise limits near residential districts, and design/siting standards. Senate amendment reportedly broadened the bill and NHMA opposed it because it would require municipalities to permit data centers on land that permits commercial or industrial uses.
key_provisions.after: Introduced SB439 would add RSA 674:81–84, with a 10 percent on-site enterprise-computing exclusion, discretionary municipal permitting in commercial/industrial zones, and utility-capacity, transit-separation, noise and design/siting conditions. The Senate-amended January 29, 2026/0176s text instead proposes RSA 674:81–83, a 25 percent on-site exclusion, data centers allowed in commercial/industrial districts subject to local land-use regulations, and planning-board rulemaking with local legislative-body approval. The compared Senate text omits the introduced prescriptive utility/noise/siting clauses. These are distinct proposed versions, not enacted zoning rights; the later House proposed amendment is not treated as adopted.

DEP, consulting BPU, would establish coverage thresholds using water use, electric demand, size, cooling/computing capacity or other resource factors; the print sets no fixed MW cutoff. The study covers preceding three- and seven-year effects, permits specified data requests and estimates, and requires a report within 15 months after an enacted effective date. These are proposed duties.

key_provisions.before: The second reprint would have required utility tariff protections for other customers against costs from commercial large-load customers at centralized facilities with aggregate monthly demand exceeding 100 MW; facilities could be aggregated based on ownership, control and infrastructure. Qualifying data centers could be covered, but the final definition was not data-center-specific.
key_provisions.after: Pocket-vetoed second reprint proposed utility tariffs for centralized commercial facilities with aggregate monthly demand over 100 MW, aggregable by ownership, control and infrastructure. Its final definition replaced the earlier data-center-specific language. Proposed safeguards included cost allocation, stranded-cost protection, financial guarantees covering at least 85% of requested service for at least 10 years, and security deposits, with BPU relaxation for sufficient operational flexibility or added energy/capacity. These failed-bill terms are not current tariff requirements.
